quote: critical ? 2 : 1
reason: Fail-closed handling blocks every Bash/PowerShell call when the PreToolUse guard itself errors; this is an operating property of the dependency/reference gate already captured in the modality of RULE-K1-0004, RULE-K1-0005, RULE-K1-0006, EXTRA-K1-0008 and EXTRA-K1-0009, not a separate engineering-outcome rule.

quote: without an exact version
reason: Suspected EXTRA (command must carry an exact version). Kept oracle-linked: DEP-003 requires choosing a verified exact stable version and avoiding floating versions; an unpinned npm add writes a caret range and an unpinned dotnet add skips explicit version selection, so the gate enforces DEP-003 without forbidding any outcome the oracle permits.
specific_behavior: Unpinned install commands are blocked until an explicit version is chosen.

quote: updates dependencies without exact versions
reason: Suspected EXTRA (bulk updates prohibited). Kept oracle-linked: DEP-003/DEP-004 require per-package latest-stable verification and due diligence for every update, which a bulk update cannot satisfy; the gate removes no outcome the oracle allows.
specific_behavior: npm update / audit fix / dotnet package update without an id are blocked.

quote: --force/--legacy-peer-deps bypasses peer-dependency resolution
reason: Suspected EXTRA because the hook blocks the flags unconditionally, while DEP-025 forbids them 'merely to bypass' peer conflicts. Kept oracle-linked: for install/update/restore verbs the flags' operative effect is peer/conflict bypass, so the gate is DEP-025 enforcement; the residual difference is noted in RULE-K1-0006 exceptions.
specific_behavior: --force on npm install/ci is blocked regardless of reason.

quote: Address each item or state why it does not apply, then finish.
reason: Suspected EXTRA (mandatory justification after production changes without tests). Kept oracle-linked for the tests reminder: it asks only to confirm coverage and probe preservation (TST-009/TST-010, verify), and permits finishing after a stated reason; the model-without-migration reminder on the same path is registered separately as EXTRA-K1-0010.
specific_behavior: Stopping is blocked once per content state until the reminder is addressed or justified.

quote: persistence code sits in `Infrastructure/Persistence/`
reason: Restates the persistence binding owned by persistence-technology.md (lines 10, 14-15); the Infrastructure/Persistence/ folder convention is an independent EXTRA owned and registered as EXTRA-K1-0016 (persistence-technology.md line 21, persistence-change line 20, persistence facet path patterns).
specific_behavior: none beyond EXTRA-K1-0016

quote: Cardinality: exactly one implementation
reason: No oracle policy defines the template's own capability-slot composition or cardinality; this constrains how the instruction system may be structured and changed (repo/meta), beyond ARC-020/DEP-009 which only require approval for new persistence or replacing approved technology.
specific_behavior: A maintainer agent may not keep two implementations of a slot, leave a required slot unfilled, or ship unselected implementations in the runtime; selecting none for frontend removes all frontend facets.

quote: An implementation must provide
reason: Template capability contracts are research/template structure, not V2 policy; they require e.g. deterministic reference checks, library checks and framework-consistency checks as part of any implementation, which no oracle policy demands.
specific_behavior: Replacing NUnit or Angular with an implementation that lacks a deterministic check facet or a scaffold facet is non-conformant and must not be accepted silently.

quote: Stable role vocabulary usable by non-slot artifacts
reason: Instruction-authoring vocabulary rule of the K1 capability design; no oracle policy restricts which technology names may appear in which instruction files.
specific_behavior: An edit to a neutral rule or workflow that hardcodes e.g. "NUnit" or "EF Core" outside the owning module violates the rule and is flagged by the structure checker.

quote: the frame binds no slot; leaves bind to it
reason: Template-structure ownership rule from the K1 capability model; the oracle prescribes no ownership location for instruction content (inventory grouping explicitly must not determine candidate structure).
specific_behavior: Template maintenance must put e.g. DbContext technique in persistence facets and test-project placement in the architecture frame, and a leaf must declare its binding.

quote: Role-named facet locations; every implementation provides exactly these (file names never change with the implementation).
reason: File-naming/location rule of the template's capability design, not derived from V2 policy.
specific_behavior: A replacement implementation must reuse e.g. rules/backend-tests/test-framework.md and scripts/facets/test-framework.cjs instead of adding implementation-named files.

quote: The framework-neutral testing standard (`.claude/rules/backend-tests/testing.md`) stays unchanged when the implementation is replaced. The knowledge facet keeps the shared skill name `dotnet-testing`.
reason: Change-procedure rule for the template's capability model; the oracle does not regulate how instruction files change when a technology is replaced.
specific_behavior: Replacing the test framework or SPA framework may only change facet files, not the neutral standards.

quote: A provider change (for example to another relational database) is a variant change inside this slot, not a new slot. Replacing the implementation (for example with a micro-ORM) requires every item below; an item the proposed implementation cannot provide — such as a migration mechanism — is surfaced as *Blocked* in the Decision Request instead of being dropped.
reason: DEP-002/ARC-020 require approval for replacing approved technology, but no oracle policy requires a contract-item completeness assessment or a Blocked marking inside the Decision Request.
specific_behavior: A Decision Request to replace EF Core with a micro-ORM must list missing items such as migrations as Blocked instead of silently omitting them.

quote: -> add-dependency workflow (removal)
reason: No oracle policy governs dependency removal (DEP-001..DEP-005 cover additions and updates); the hook makes every removal command fail via the shell regardless of approval.
specific_behavior: `npm uninstall lodash` or `dotnet remove package Foo` is blocked (exit 2) even when the user asked for the removal; removal must follow the add-dependency workflow.

quote: changes the project reference graph (${f.edges.map(e => `${e.from} -> ${e.to}`).join(', ') || 'unnamed project'}), a Reserved decision without a recorded approval
reason: ARC-001 already permits inward references (Api -> Application, Infrastructure -> Application) and ARC-020 requires approval for consequential changes such as new layers/projects; no oracle policy requires a recorded, dated approval for each individual reference edge, including standard inward or narrow test references.
specific_behavior: Scaffolding the standard Clean Architecture references or adding an Application.Tests -> Application reference is blocked or flagged until an accepted decision lists the edge.

quote: Address each item or state why it does not apply, then finish.
reason: The oracle requires a migration only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes (PST-009) and review of generated migrations (PST-010); it contains no general duty that every model change be checked for schema impact and paired with a migration, nor a stop-time confirmation.
specific_behavior: Editing a Domain entity without adding a migration blocks the stop once until the agent confirms whether the schema changed.

quote: they are the natural repository-boundary candidates
reason: Considered as a hidden repository-per-aggregate rule. Rejected: the sentence is descriptive ('natural candidates'), conditional on an already approved DDD design, and imposes no obligation or prohibition.
specific_behavior: none

quote: unless the approved specification already requires them
reason: Suspected relaxation EXTRA (approval waived when the specification requires DDD). Kept oracle-linked: an approved specification is itself an approval of the required behavior (GOV-001), so ARC-004's approval requirement is satisfied rather than relaxed.
specific_behavior: Rich-domain patterns demanded by the approved specification need no separate approval.

quote: a `VersionOverride` needs a recorded reason
reason: Suspected EXTRA (recorded reason for VersionOverride). Kept oracle-linked: DEP-006 says PackageReference entries are 'normally' versionless; requiring a reason for the exceptional override specifies the 'normally' qualifier without forbidding any oracle-permitted outcome.
specific_behavior: A VersionOverride without a stated reason is non-conformant.

quote: In an established project that deliberately uses another framework, follow that convention
reason: Suspected relaxation EXTRA. Kept oracle-linked: TST-001 is a DEFAULT and RUN-009 makes repository conventions authoritative, so following a deliberately chosen existing framework is within the oracle.
specific_behavior: In a project already using xUnit deliberately, xUnit continues to be used.

quote: `package.json` and `package-lock.json` must be committed and kept consistent
reason: Suspected EXTRA (lockfile must be committed). Kept oracle-linked: DEP-007 requires a consistent package-lock and WF-018 presumes a maintained lockfile; 'committed' means version-controlled, not an instruction to run git commit (GOV-015 still governs commits).
specific_behavior: The lockfile is kept under source control.

quote: application-level HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection is not required
reason: Suspected relaxation EXTRA. Kept oracle-linked: SEC-007 itself requires respecting the actual hosting topology; waiving app-level redirection where the deployment provides the secure boundary is that same qualifier.
specific_behavior: App-level HTTPS redirection may be omitted behind TLS-terminating infrastructure.

quote: product inputs never override policy
reason: Initially registered as LINK_UNCERTAIN (does policy outrank an approved specification, restricting GOV-001?). Resolved after reading the always-loaded owner CLAUDE.md line 24: inputs 'may request a decision change' but 'must not silently override engineering policy or recorded decisions', and CLAUDE.md line 30 classifies what the specification already requires as Decided. That is GOV-017 decision control, not a restriction of GOV-001; the map's unqualified 'never' is a not-loaded summary with no separate runtime effect.
specific_behavior: A specification or task that conflicts with a recorded decision triggers a Decision Request instead of a silent override.

quote: Three coordinates classify every artifact, asked in this order:
reason: Instruction-system classification scheme of the K1 design; no oracle policy dictates how instruction artifacts are classified, headed or located.
specific_behavior: A new rule or skill must be placed and headed according to its Capability/Kind/Scope classification; misplacement is a structural error.

quote: Dependency direction: WF → KNW → STD → DEC → OP; ENF → STD/DEC, declared on each ENF artifact's `Conforms:` line (the line after its header); product inputs never override policy. reason: Internal dependency discipline of the instruction system, not derived from any V2 policy.

quote: any artifact is added, moved, or removed
reason: Research construction principle (one normative owner) realised as an instruction-maintenance rule; not one of the 196 V2 policies.
specific_behavior: Adding a duplicate rule in a second file or adding an artifact without updating MAP.md is non-conformant (checked by the structure checker).

quote: Dependency direction: WF → KNW → STD → DEC → OP; ENF → STD/DEC, declared on each ENF artifact's `Conforms:` line (the line after its header); product inputs never override policy. reason: GOV-017 makes Reserved changes approval-gated but does not make the template's own slot contracts Reserved or route instruction changes through a user-invoked maintenance workflow.

quote: - Must not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it only when published compatibility or coexistence of client generations creates a concrete need (adopting versioning: Reserved, `CLAUDE.md`).
reason: API-013 only forbids versioning without a concrete need and DEP-017 makes the package conditional; neither requires explicit approval to adopt versioning once a concrete need exists, and ARC-020's approval list does not include API versioning.

reason: PST-003 requires a dedicated internal seeder surface and ARC-019 keeps EF Core in Infrastructure, but no oracle policy fixes folder paths; the candidate binds concrete folders and its Stop-hook reminders only recognise these paths.
specific_behavior: A seeder placed outside Infrastructure/Persistence/Seeding/ is non-conformant and is not recognised by the seed co-change reminder.

quote: if (!manifests.isApprovedProject(approvals, name)) changes.push(`project ${name} added`);
reason: Suspected EXTRA (recorded approval for project addition/removal). Unlike EXTRA-K1-0009, it gates no outcome the oracle leaves free.

reason: Structural self-validation of the instruction system; no oracle policy constrains instruction-file structure.

reason: Loading/organization rule of the K1 instruction system; no V2 policy regulates rule-file layout or globs.

reason: Context-budget rule of the template design; not a V2 policy.

reason: Suspected EXTRA (frontend prohibition). Kept oracle-linked: API-010 keeps Domain invariants at their owning boundary and FE-010 limits frontend validation to UX; the exception for equivalent user-facing rules mirrors FE-010.

quote: do not test framework internals
reason: Suspected EXTRA because oracle TST policies are scoped to backend-tests. Kept oracle-linked: TST-002/TST-003 normalized wording is stack-neutral (behavior over implementation details, narrowest meaningful level) and the clause applies it to frontend tests without adding a new restriction.
specific_behavior: Frontend tests avoid framework internals and duplicate coverage.

quote: Investigate deliberate bypasses
reason: Considered as a hidden review obligation. Rejected as non-normative: investigation prompts in on-demand knowledge, comparable to the oracle's own exclusion of scan-layer prompts (EXC-015); no outcome is required or forbidden.
specific_behavior: none

quote: Permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD-family licenses may normally be accepted
reason: Suspected relaxation EXTRA (pre-approved license classes). Kept oracle-linked: DEP-005 requires approval only for paid/commercial or materially restrictive/unclear licenses; accepting permissive licenses is the complement of that rule.

quote: never referenced from Domain
reason: DEP-011 approves Mapster when mapping volume warrants it and ARC-002 keeps Domain free of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service concerns; no oracle policy forbids a mapping library in Domain.

quote: Remove dependencies that are no longer used when doing so is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead package references behind, and do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task.
reason: No oracle policy requires removing packages made unused by a change (RUN-010 covers only unused usings in changed C# files); the candidate adds a cleanup obligation.

quote: Build and run the affected tests (`verify`). Report: package, version, license, due-diligence results, and any approval obtained or pending.
reason: WF-009 requires reporting what verification actually ran; no oracle policy requires reporting package, version, license and due-diligence outcomes for each dependency change.
specific_behavior: The final report of a dependency change must list license and due-diligence results.

quote: only as a consistent project-level decision
reason: Suspected relaxation/condition EXTRA. Kept oracle-linked: API-011 forbids establishing business exceptions as the default architecture; permitting typed exceptions only as a deliberate, consistent project decision keeps that boundary.
specific_behavior: Ad-hoc typed business exceptions are not used; a project-wide decision may adopt them for selected cases.

quote: If adopted, use typed errors rather than string arrays
reason: Considered as an extra mandatory pattern. Rejected as technique: it only shapes the representation inside an already approved Result model and restricts no outcome the oracle governs.

reason: Suspected EXTRA. Kept oracle-linked: changing declared platform versions to suit a local machine is an out-of-scope behavior change (GOV-014) and DEP-008 fixes the platform baseline; reporting the limitation is WF-009.
specific_behavior: Toolchain mismatch is reported, not patched by editing versions.

quote: 2. For a consequential or non-obvious decision, add `docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md` (context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, date, approver).
reason: GOV-017 requires approval of Reserved changes and GOV-007 synchronization of approved product rules, but no oracle policy requires a separate architecture decision record with fixed content.

quote: List the decision, its class, approval source, register/record updates, and any request still unresolved.
reason: Reporting duty specific to the decision workflow; WF-009 covers verification reporting only.

quote: do not add deprecated/legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration packages
reason: DEP-010 makes FluentValidation the standard library but prescribes no registration package; no oracle policy forbids the ASP.NET automatic-validation integration packages outright (DEP-004 only requires a deprecation check).

quote: Never cache tracked persistence entities across Unit of Work boundaries.
reason: RUN-021 governs invalidation consistency and ARC-017 the shared scoped context, but no oracle policy forbids caching tracked entities across Unit of Work scopes.
specific_behavior: A cache storing EF-tracked entity instances for reuse by later requests is prohibited.

quote: Breaking changes and adopting versioning are Reserved
reason: Suspected EXTRA for breaking changes. Kept oracle-linked for breaking changes: API-014 already requires a new version or an explicitly approved compatibility strategy; only the versioning-adoption part is extra (EXTRA-K1-0017).
specific_behavior: Breaking a published contract requires approval.

quote: update this section when the solution structure changes
reason: Considered as a maintenance obligation. Rejected: Dockerfile-shape guidance inside conditional container technique (the class the oracle excludes, EXC-006); it constrains no engineering outcome beyond keeping the example consistent.

reason: Reporting duty specific to the workflow; WF-009 requires reporting verification state only, not a per-setting surface inventory.

reason: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification state; the duty to report the change rationale, approvals and every unresolved Decision Request is an additional reporting obligation.

quote: Do not claim idempotency because duplicates are merely unlikely

specific_behavior: none

reason: Considered as an extra messaging rule. Rejected as conditional resilience technique (message-delivery examples, EXC-007); no messaging is part of the baseline.

quote: - **Never fire-and-forget** EF Core asynchronous operations; a `DbContext` is not thread-safe.
reason: RUN-002 forbids blocking async I/O and ARC-022 governs DI lifetimes; no oracle policy forbids un-awaited (fire-and-forget) database operations or concurrent DbContext use.
specific_behavior: Starting an EF Core query without awaiting it (e.g. background Task.Run over the request DbContext) is prohibited.

Do not apply HTTP retry policies to database operations.
reason: RUN-016 limits retries to safe operations and DEP-020 sets the default resilience packages, but no oracle policy prescribes provider-level execution strategies or forbids application-level retry pipelines for database calls (the oracle treats database-retry examples as technique, EXC-007).

reason: Open question: GOV-015 permits repository-changing Git operations only when explicitly requested; whether 'clearly required by an approved workflow' merely refers to a workflow the user explicitly requested (entailed) or lets a workflow trigger destructive operations without a specific request (a relaxation) is not determinable from the text.

reason: GOV-015 allows force-push and other history-changing operations when explicitly requested; declaring main/master non-rewritable is stricter (read literally, even an explicit request does not unlock rewriting them).

reason: PST-009 requires updating provider-sensitive tests only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes and TST-007 governs provider fidelity, not when tests must be added; no oracle policy obliges new or updated tests for every mapping/constraint/query change.
